chunks: And Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hashim, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) mentioned the Qaim (peace be upon him) and said: 'He will be hidden from them, so that the ignorant will say: What does Allah need with the Family of Muhammad?'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الْجَاهِل: The ignorant one, referring to those lacking deep religious knowledge
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the occultation of the Qaim and the reaction of the ignorant?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the 'Test of the Shia' during the Major Occultation, where the prolonged absence of the Imam leads the ignorant (*al-jahil*) to question the divine necessity of the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the theological concept that the Imam’s hidden presence remains essential for Allah’s purposes, even when his guidance is not visibly manifest to the masses.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 290 - Narrated Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik Kufi from Ishaq bin Muhammad bin Abu Hashim from Furat bin Ahnaf that he said:
Amirul Momineen (a.s) mentioned the Qaim (a.s) and said: “He will go into hiding, so the ignorant will say that Allah does not have any need of Aale Muhammad (a.s).”
